_README: The gallery is a GRAPH, not a space. Each room is described on its own and
knows nothing of the others; a doorway just names the room it leads to. That is
the whole trick behind the impossible geometry — nothing is ever checked for
global consistency, because there is no global space to be consistent with.
Four rooms can each be one flight UP from the last and still close into a loop.
Adding a room is an entry here. Adding art to a wall is one string.
ROOM
name       shown in the HUD on arrival
note       optional line of text, for a room that wants to say something
size       [width, height, depth] in metres-ish. 4x3x4 is a normal room.
surfaces   floor, ceiling, north, east, west — all optional. "south" is
BEHIND the viewer and is never drawn, so put art on the other
five; a "south" exit still works as a button in the HUD.
SURFACE
art        what is on it (see ART below). Optional.
frame      true to hang it as a framed piece rather than cover the surface
exit       room id this surface leads to. Makes a doorway.
label      text on the doorway
ascend     flights climbed by taking it (negative to descend). The HUD keeps
a running total, so a staircase that loops proves it is impossible.
repeat     tile the art N times across the surface (for patterns)
ART — one string, resolved in this order:
work:<id>        a work from media.json (video loop, or its poster)
shader:<id>      a live shader from shaders/manifest.json — real WebGL on the
wall. 'shader:random' picks one per visit.
image:<path>     any image in the repo
pattern:<name>   a generated tessellation, drawn in code, so rooms look right
before any art exists. hex, penrose, triangle, escher, moire, grid
color:<css>      a flat colour
Nothing here is required. A room with no art still works; a missing asset
leaves the surface bare rather than breaking the gallery.
THE FRACTAL
Past the authored rooms the gallery is endless. A room id like "f012" is
an ADDRESS: each digit picks one of the contractive maps in "fractal.maps",
so the digits walk deeper into their attractor. The room's size, colour,
patterns and name all come from the orbit at that point, which makes it
deterministic (an address is always the same room) and self-similar
(addresses sharing a prefix are near each other, so a room resembles its
parent). Edit "maps" and the whole endless half of the gallery changes.
